title: Single Agent Robust Deep Reinforcement Learning for Bus Fleet Control
abstract: arXiv:2508.20784v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Bus bunching remains a challenge for urban transit due to stochastic traffic and passenger demand. Traditional solutions rely on multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) in loop-line settings, which overlook realistic operations characterized by heterogeneous routes, timetables, fluctuating demand, and varying fleet sizes. We propose a novel single-agent reinforcement learning (RL) framework for bus holding control that avoids the data imbalance and convergence issues of MARL under near-realistic simulation. A bidirectional timetabled network with dynamic passenger demand is constructed. The key innovation is reformulating the multi-agent problem into a single-agent one by augmenting the state space with categorical identifiers (vehicle ID, station ID, time period) in addition to numerical features (headway, occupancy, velocity). This high-dimensional encoding enables single-agent policies to capture inter-agent dependencies, analog

translated_title: 面向公交车队控制的单智能体鲁棒深度强化学习
translated_abstract: 由于交通状况和乘客需求的随机性，公交串车问题一直是城市公共交通面临的挑战。传统解决方案依赖于环形线路场景下的多智能体强化学习（MARL），这忽视了现实运营中所具有的异构线路、时刻表、需求波动和车队规模变化等特征。我们提出了一种新颖的单智能体强化学习（RL）框架用于公交车驻站控制，避免了MARL在近现实仿真中存在的数据不平衡和收敛问题。该研究构建了一个具有动态乘客需求的双向时刻表公交网络。其关键创新在于，通过在数值特征（车头时距、载客率、速度）之外增加分类标识符（车辆ID、站点ID、时间段）来增广状态空间，从而将多智能体问题重新表述为单智能体问题。这种高维编码使单智能体策略能够捕捉智能体之间的相互依赖关系（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出一种单智能体深度强化学习框架，通过在状态空间中引入车辆ID、站点ID、时间段等分类标识符并结合车头时距、载客率等数值特征，将多智能体公交驻站控制问题重新表述为单智能体问题，在考虑时刻表、动态乘客需求和可变车队规模的近现实双向网络仿真中有效避免了MARL的数据不平衡与收敛问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a single-agent deep reinforcement learning framework that reformulates the multi-agent bus holding control problem into a single-agent one by augmenting the state space with categorical identifiers (vehicle ID, station ID, time period) alongside numerical features (headway, occupancy, velocity), thereby avoiding the data imbalance and convergence issues of MARL under near-realistic simulations featuring timetables, dynamic passenger demand, and varying fleet sizes.
